videos.t: Gallerydrive presentation setup at UdK Berlin
videos.desc: Gallerydrive is an automatic system to experience art exhibitions. Visitors are driven through the show on line following electric vehicles. This Video shows an intermediate presentation setup of the system. The system is developed by Niklas Roy (Royrobotiks) and the artist group //////////fur////. Please find out more at www.cyberniklas.de/gallerydrive

videos.t: International Dance Party - The crazy nerd radar dance!
videos.desc:
This is an engineering test of the "International Dance PArty's" internal dance activity radar system.

Check out www.internationaldanceparty.com to find out more about this crazy machine.

videos.t: International Dance Party - Hardware  test & presentation
videos.desc:
In this Video, Niklas Roy presents the core hardware for the crazy machine, called "International Dance Party".

He does this in his Royrobotiks studio in Berlin.

videos.t: International Dance Party - Fog latch engineering test
videos.desc:
This is an another piece of amazing technology, presented by Niklas Roy, CEO of Royrobotiks. 
In this engineering test, he shows the IDP's fog latch. To find more about the crazy machine called "International Dance Party", click www.internationaldanceparty.com

videos.t: International Dance PArty - Light FX lifting mechanism test
videos.desc:
This is another video of an IDP hardware test.

To find out more about the crazy machine, called "International Dance Party" - check www.internationaldanceparty.com

The interactive machine "International Dance Party" is a complete party in a box. With its internal radar, the machine senses and evaluates dance activity of surrounding people and transforms into a mobile disco the more the audience dances.

Visit www.internationaldanceparty.com for more information.
This remote controlled walking ladder is another handy device of Niklas Roy. Find more interresting machines, gadgets, devices and installations on his webpage www.cyberniklas.de

videos.t: Autohonk - Automatically honking car tuning device
videos.desc:
If you have to brake - honking can't be wrong.
The Autohonk is a nifty little apparatus which lets a car honk automatically as soon as the driver pushes the brake pedal. 
Find other interresting machines and devices on www.cyberniklas.de

You have to see this! It's a crazy party machine, called "International Dance Party". The machine comes as a flightcase, but transforms itself automatically into a complete disco. No fake! 

The whole thing is controlled by a radar sensor, which detects how much people dance. The more they dance, the more it transforms.

Based on the incoming activity data (from the radar), the music is automatically generated.

Check also the website: www.internationaldanceparty.com and see the full length video!

videos.t: Perpetual motion energy production that really works!
videos.desc:
Energy production by utilizing perpetual motion technologies has always been a fundamental dream of mankind. Global energy crisis and an increasing awareness of environmental issues demand new research in this particular field of physics. Royrobotiks Sustainability Research Division suggests an easy way to save the future of mother earth and to reduce your private electric bill to zero. 
The suggested perpetual motion setup can be easily made out of normal household materials and it takes less than a minute to get it successfully running, as this demonstration video will show you.

An attempt in shifting Google Earths virtual 3D representation of my neighbourhood. All models and textures are slightly altered versions of their real counterparts.

The models in the video above were built with Sketchup and submitted to Google, where a jury will decide if they appear in Google Earths 3D layer. The model of my workshop (big "R" in front / yellow inside) is already accepted by Google and can be viewed in Google Maps ("Earth"-function) or in the Google Earth browser. 

Just enter "Scheffelstrasse 9, Berlin", switch on the 3D layer and enjoy!

videos.t: Headpong with Windows on the green meadow
videos.desc:
This video shows a pong-like tennis game that uses a laptop's internal webcam as game controller. The computer detects people's faces and moves their players according to their real head positions. Download this game at http://www.niklasroy.com/articles/98/headpong-download
The music is composed and produced by Holy Konni http://www.freizeitmeister.org

PING is a low-tech augmented reality videogame that overlays a moving pixel to a videosignal. The pixel bounces off from objects that are darker than a specific threshold value. More about this projects at http://www.niklasroy.com/project/101/PING

This camera is a connection of a thermal receipt printer and a b/w video camera. The device prints photos directly on receipt paper. You can find more information about it on my webpage: http://www.niklasroy.com/project/103/electronic_instant_camera

"Wasserklang Modulsystem" is a water powered multichannel sound installation.
A big water wheel in the forge of Berlin's Technikmuseum drives eight mechanical music boxes, each playing a different song. They are connected by a several hundred meter long rope which makes a zig-zag course through the little forest and alongside the rail track.

The installation was produced by La belle Imira and Niklas Roy for Berlin's Museum Night 2011. 

http://www.niklasroy.com/project/110/wasserklang-modulsystem

The answer is here: http://www.niklasroy.com/project/116/Lumenoise

videos.t: Ping Pong Country / Edition Sabotage / Hotel Europa / Lille
videos.desc:
Ping Pong Country / Sabotage is an environment in which many people play ping pong while listening to country music. Another person can sabotage the game in various ways via a master control desk.

The installation is part of 2012's Hotel Europa at Lille's Gare St. Sauveur. You can rent this room for free together with your friends until August 12th, 2012. Place your reservation here: http://www.lille3000.eu/gare-saint-sauveur/printemps-2012/hotel-europa

The installation was made by Remco Schuurbiers, Bijan Dawallu and Niklas Roy.

More info on the room can be found here: http://www.niklasroy

Wind powered umbrella turbines produce sound and soap bubbles. 
This video shows a test of the construction on a rooftop in Berlin. The installation will be built in large - with many of those umbrellaphones - at "Prototype 1" festival in Sao Paulo in November 2012. 
http://www.niklasroy.com/articles/133/umbrellaphone-umbrellabubble

"Hammer Synthesizer" is multiphonic eight channel 1Bit synthesizer, built into a log of wood. The synthesizer is played by hitting felt balls (covered with conductive yarn) with a hammer. Schematics and code are available at http://www.niklasroy.com/articles/134/hammer-synthesizer

The "Perpetual Energy Wasting Machine" is a rope and pulley mechanism which moves an elevator continuously between the 1st and 2nd floor of a building. The system is powered by the sliding doors of the elevator. 

http://www.niklasroy.com/project/137/perpetual_energy_wasting_machine

The installation was created during a residency at the WRO Art Center in Wroclaw, Poland. It was funded by the Goethe Institute Cracow.

http://www.niklasroy.com/project/149/cardboard_plotter
This plotter is made entirely out of cardboard, welding rod, rubber bands, adhesive tape and super glue. The digital memory is a little book with plenty of different drawing codes, which are written down as coordinates. In this video I'm entering the first code, which makes the plotter draw "hello world".

videos.t: Pneumatic Sponge Ball Accelerator at Tschumi Pavilion / Groningen
videos.desc:
The "Pneumatic Sponge Ball Accelerator" is installed at the Tschumi Pavilion in Groningen / The Netherlands. The apparatus contains 1000 black sponge balls, which are sucked through 150m of transparent pneumatic tubes with the power of a normal household vacuum cleaner. Visitors can operate the machine with a touch sensor: They can change the direction of the airflow and watch the balls speed up, slow down and turn around. The balls reach a top speed of about 4m/s.

You can read more about the project on my website: http://www.niklasroy.com/project/174/PSBA

The Forbidden Fruit Machine is an interactive installation made by Kati Hyyppä and Niklas Roy. It is based on a painting called "The Fall of Man" created by Cornelis Cornelisz. van Haarlem in 1592. The machine reinterprets the historical artwork in the form of a mechatronic video game, giving the spectator of the painting the chance to control the destiny of the forbidden apple with a joystick. The image of the painting used as a basis of the machine is from the Rijksmuseum's public domain image collection and the sounds used in the special effects are from the open collections of the Internet

videos.t: "J'ai faim!" - A Mechatronic game by Kati Hyyppä & Niklas Roy
videos.desc:
“J’ai faim!” is french for “I’m hungry!” and it is a mechatronic game that deals with eating. Just like Barbie, we here in Europe live a luxurious life where there is no lack of food – quite the contrary. Yet extra calories seem like a sin and many aspire for an unnaturally slender figure in the hope of looking more attractive. Considering how many people actually have to struggle for their daily nourishment, this seems bizarre. “J’ai faim!” is all about making Barbie to eat more and be happy about food. If she doesn’t keep eating, the game is over.

The game was made as a part of MalakoNiarof

videos.t: Wasserorgel von Winnenden - Pressure washer powered musical fountain
videos.desc:
Project page: https://niklasroy.com/wasserorgelvonwinnenden/

The "Wasserorgel von Winnenden" is a musical fountain, powered by eight pressure washers and controlled by an electronic keyboard. Passers-by are invited to play some tunes on the keyboard and the Wasserorgel responds with a magical water and light show. The machine memorizes each keystroke and repeats random melody fragments, when nobody is interacting with it.

The music is Concerto No. 1 in E major, Op. 8, RV 269, "La primavera" (Spring) — Movement 1: Allegro from The Four Seasons by Antonio Vivaldi, performed and recorded by John Harrison (http://johnharrisonviolin.com/).

"Bootlabor" (Boat laboratory) was a kids workshop at Werkraum Schöpflin in Lörrach in 2018.

More info on Kati's website: http://katihyyppa.com/bootlabor/

Art-in-Architecture project for Schulzentrum Südwest in Nuremberg, Germany.

The project reimagines the traditional school bell: Students compose their own melodies, which are then stored in an archive. Each time the bell rings, a random composition is selected and performed by a physical instrument.
Complementing the sound is a custom clock where the hands "dance" in synchronization with the melodies. This video is a functional demo of that mechanical choreography.

Follow the progress in my project diary: https://niklasroy.com/diary/index.html?tagName=Schulgong

“Glashütte Trash Clock” is a fully functioning clockwork made from trash and other stuff that I found in Glashütte, Saxony. Since the mechanism just runs for about half an hour, it only displays just seconds and minutes, striking a gong whenever the minute hand reaches the 12 o’clock position. As a little extra, the clock also triggers an external randomizer just before it runs out of energy.

While working on this clock, I also invented a new time scale: GTC. It blends the concepts of GMT and UTC, and the Glashütte Trash Clock serves as its global reference clock.
